speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing acute diarrhea; to help me diagnose the cause, how long have your symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: *Clostridioides difficile* infection (C. diff).

Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin for pneumonia and the onset of frequent watery diarrhea with cramping, this strongly suggests a complication from your antibiotic therapy. I need to confirm if you have noticed any fever, blood in your stool, or recent hospital stays. REQUEST TEST: C. difficile toxin assay.
